mainTopic: Learning from a קנס, and the liability of one who shows or hands over another's property to oppressors, ending with the story of רב כהנא
overview: The amud opens by asking whether רב נחמן's earlier ruling was a real דין or only a קנס, because we never learn other cases from a קנס. The גמרא tries to prove this rule from a ברייתא about damage you cannot see (מטמא, מנסך, מדמע). It rejects the proof twice: once by pointing to the size of the loss, and once by a change from רבי אבין's view to רבי ירמיה's view. Next come cases of a Jew who shows or hands another Jew's property to gentile authorities. Being forced and only showing is פטור. Handing it over yourself, or showing it on your own, is חייב. רב אשי adds that once the property was already exposed, carrying it afterward adds nothing. In a dispute over a net, רבא rules that the one who handed it to the king's officer is put in שמתא until he brings it back to court. The amud ends with the story of רב כהנא, who killed an informer, fled to ארץ ישראל, and met רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Was the ruling law or a penalty?
steps.stepSummary: The question is whether רב נחמן's ruling that someone must pay was the actual דין or a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was it the real law, or was it a fine?
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes a question about רב נחמן's earlier ruling that someone had to pay. The question is whether he ruled that way because it is the real דין, or as a קנס to punish bad behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דין means the person truly owes the money by law. A קנס is an extra penalty the חכמים impose even though strict law might not require payment. The question sets up the next step, which explains why the difference matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The actual law, what is truly owed
A fine or penalty imposed by the חכמים

phrases.english: Is it the law, or is it a fine?
phrases.notes: "It" means רב נחמן's earlier ruling making the person pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question about רב נחמן's ruling that began on the previous amud
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב נחמן's ruling was based on the actual law or was a penalty

steps.title: Why it matters: we cannot learn from a fine
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling is a דין, we apply it to other cases. If it is a קנס, we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is the law, we learn from it. If it is a fine, we do not learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains the practical difference behind the question. A real דין can be applied to similar cases, but a קנס cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is a special decision made for a specific situation, so we cannot assume the חכמים meant to apply it anywhere else. A דין is a general rule, so it works for any similar case.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn from it and apply it to other cases

steps.whatToRemember: We do not learn other cases from a קנס, only from a דין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that a קנס is not stretched to other cases, comes up again and again in monetary halacha.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If it is the law, we learn from it;
if it is a fine, we do not learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי דִּינָא – גָּמְרִינַן מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by explaining why it matters
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דין can be applied to other cases; a קנס cannot

steps.title: Where do we know we can't learn from a fine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the rule that we do not learn from a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that we do not learn from a fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the rule just stated. This sets up the next step, where a ברייתא is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 2 sounded logical, but the גמרא wants a real source that shows it. The next steps try to supply one.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you say this? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that we do not learn from a fine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in the answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that we do not learn other cases from a קנס

steps.title: A ברייתא about damage you cannot see
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that at first the חכמים made the מטמא and the מנסך pay, and later they added the מדמע too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: At first they would say that one who makes another's food impure and one who pours another's wine for idol worship must pay. Later they went back and said: also one who mixes תרומה into another's produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing people who must pay for damage that does not show on the object. The list grew over time: first two cases, then a third was added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all three cases the item looks the same, but it has become forbidden or less useful. The key detail for the proof is that the third case, מדמע, needed to be added on its own. The next step builds the proof from that.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes another's food impure
One who pours another's wine as an offering to idols, making it forbidden
One who mixes תרומה into another's regular produce, so non-כהנים may not eat it
As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught: At first they would say:
one who makes impure and one who pours a libation [must pay];
phrases.notes: The words "must pay" are not written here, but the ברייתא assumes them. Both cases ruin another person's food or wine.

phrases.english: they later went back and said: also one who mixes in תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that will be used as the proof
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we do not learn from a קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא listing מטמא, מנסך, and later מדמע

steps.title: Drawing the proof from the added case
steps.stepSummary: Since מדמע needed to be added separately, the גמרא suggests it is because these payments are a קנס, and we cannot learn from a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only because they went back and added it, yes he pays. If they had not added it, no. Why? Isn't it because this payment is a fine, and we do not learn from a fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the proof clear. If the חכמים had to add מדמע separately, it shows we could not learn it from מטמא and מנסך on our own, and the reason must be that those payments are a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדמע seems just like the other two cases, since the damage is not visible. If those payments were a דין, we would apply them to מדמע automatically. Needing a new ruling suggests they are a קנס, and a קנס does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: Since they went back and added it, yes
Is it not because...? (introduces a suggested reason)

phrases.english: They went back and added it, yes; had they not added it, no.
What is the reason?
Is it not because it is a fine,
and from a fine we do not learn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא to draw the proof
steps.raayaObject: We do not learn other cases from a קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that מדמע had to be added on its own and was not learned from מטמא and מנסך

steps.title: No: the change was about small losses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. At first the חכמים only cared about a big loss. Later they decided to care about a small loss too.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. At first they held that the חכמים were concerned about a big loss and not about a small loss. In the end they held that they were concerned about a small loss too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The reason מדמע was added later has nothing to do with קנס. It is because its loss is smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making food impure or forbidden for benefit is a big loss. Mixing in תרומה is a smaller loss, since the produce can still be sold, just for less. The חכמים first made people pay only for big losses and later for small losses too, so the ברייתא does not prove the rule about קנס.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, the later addition of מדמע came because the חכמים came to care about small losses too, not because of a קנס. The next step challenges this answer.
steps.confusionAlert: The rejection does not cancel the rule that we do not learn from a קנס. It only says this ברייתא is not the proof for it.

phrases.english: No; at first they held:
they were concerned about a big loss,
they were not concerned about a small loss;
phrases.notes: The small loss is the מדמע case. The produce can still be sold, just to fewer buyers.

phrases.english: and in the end they held:
they were concerned about a small loss as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not the rule about קנס itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The later addition of מדמע can be explained by the size of the loss, not by the payment being a קנס

steps.title: A second version of the ברייתא flips the order
steps.stepSummary: The father of רבי אבין taught the ברייתא differently: first the מטמא and the מדמע, and later the מנסך was added. This undoes the 'big loss versus small loss' answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? The father of רבי אבין taught: at first they said the one who makes food impure and the one who mixes in תרומה must pay. Later they added the one who pours wine for idol worship too. So only because they added him later is he liable; without that, he would not be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 6 by quoting a different version of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6 we said the חכמים started with big losses and later added small ones. But in this version the מנסך, which causes a big loss, is the one added later. So the 'big loss first' answer cannot explain this version.

keyTerms.meaning: One who pours someone else's wine as an offering to idols

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first ברייתא the מדמע was added later. Here the מנסך is added later. That switch is the whole challenge.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't the father of Rabbi Avin teach:
At first they would say:
one who makes impure and one who mixes in teruma [must pay];
they later said: also the one who pours a libation.
Since they added it, yes; had they not added it, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא תָּנֵי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Step 6 with another version of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 6 answer that the חכמים first cared only about big losses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this version the big-loss case (מנסך) was added later, so 'big loss first' cannot be the reason.

steps.title: So the reason must be that we cannot learn from a קנס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the מנסך needed to be added separately and suggests it is because we do not learn one קנס from another.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the מנסך had to be added on its own? Is it not because we do not learn from a קנס?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the new version, the גמרא brings back the proof from Step 5: the separate addition shows we cannot learn from a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the payment were a regular דין, the מנסך could have been learned from the first two cases. Since the big-loss answer no longer works, the best explanation seems to be that a קנס cannot be extended.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not because...? (suggests an answer)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because we do not learn from a fine?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא גָּמְרִינַן מִקְּנָסָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the version quoted in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we do not learn from a קנס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the father of רבי אבין, where the מנסך was added later.

steps.title: No, the חכמים changed from רבי אבין's view to רבי ירמיה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. At first the חכמים held like רבי אבין, and in the end they held like רבי ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. At first they held like רבי אבין, and in the end they held like רבי ירמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof and gives another reason the מנסך was added later. It names two opinions and will explain them next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later addition was not about a קנס. It came from a real change of opinion. At first the חכמים followed a view that exempts the מנסך from paying, and later they followed a view that makes him pay.

phrases.english: No;
at first they held like Rabbi Avin,
and in the end they held like Rabbi Yirmeya.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; מֵעִיקָּרָא סָבְרִי כְּרַבִּי אָבִין, וּלְבַסּוֹף סָבְרִי כְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the later addition proves we cannot learn from a קנס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The addition can be explained by a change of opinion about whether the מנסך is exempt at all.

steps.title: רבי אבין's rule: the arrow on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין teaches that if someone shoots an arrow four אמות on שבת and it tears silk along the way, he is exempt from paying, since the whole flight is one act that makes him liable to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they held like רבי אבין, who said: If someone shot an arrow from the start of four אמות to the end of four אמות, and on its way it tore silk, he is exempt from paying. This is because lifting the arrow is part of putting it down, and he is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first opinion from Step 9 by quoting רבי אבין's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The arrow's whole flight counts as one act of carrying on שבת, which brings the death penalty. When one act brings both death and a money payment, the person gets only the death penalty and does not pay. The same idea exempts the מנסך, since pouring for idols also brings the death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: Four אמות, the distance for the carrying מלאכה in a public area
Lifting an object from its place
He is liable to the death penalty

steps.whatToRemember: The מנסך was added later not because of a קנס rule. At first the חכמים followed רבי אבין, who exempts someone from paying when the same act makes him liable to death.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the idea that the later addition came from a change of opinion, so the ברייתא no longer proves that we cannot learn from a קנס.

phrases.english: At first they held like Rabbi Avin –
as Rabbi Avin said:

phrases.aramaic: זָרַק חֵץ מִתְּחִילַּת אַרְבַּע לְסוֹף אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: If one shot an arrow from the start of four [cubits] to the end of four,
phrases.notes: He means four אמות in a public area on שבת, the distance that counts as carrying.

phrases.english: and it tore silks on its way – he is exempt;
since the lifting is a necessary part of the placing,
and he is liable with his life.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא סָבְרִי כְּרַבִּי אָבִין – דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the answer in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who damages during an act of שבת carrying that brings the death penalty is exempt from paying, because the lifting and placing are one act.

steps.title: The later view: money liability comes before the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: In the end the חכמים held like רבי ירמיה. The thief owes money from the moment he lifts the wine, but he is only liable to death when he pours it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end they held like רבי ירמיה, because רבי ירמיה said: from the moment he lifts the wine he acquires it and owes the owner money. He is not liable to death until the moment he pours it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the rejection from step 9 by explaining רבי ירמיה's view, which the חכמים came to accept later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין held that the money debt and the death penalty come together, so there is no payment. רבי ירמיה splits them in time: the debt starts at lifting and the death penalty only at pouring. Since the two do not happen at once, the מנסך must pay. That explains why the מנסך was added to the ברייתא only later.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting; an act that makes the item legally his
Liable with his life (to the death penalty)
Pouring wine as an offering to עבודה זרה

steps.whatToRemember: Lifting the wine already makes him owe money, before the pouring makes him liable to death. Because the two happen at different times, the מנסך pays.

phrases.english: And in the end they held like Rabbi Yirmeya
as Rabbi Yirmeya said:
From the time of lifting, he acquires it,
and he becomes obligated to him for money;
liable with his life he is not
until the time of pouring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 10 explained רבי אבין's early view. This step explains רבי ירמיה's later view and closes the rejection from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The money debt starts at lifting and the death penalty only at pouring, so the two do not happen together and the מנסך must pay.

steps.title: רב הונא בר יהודה reports a case he judged
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה tells רבא about a Jew who was forced by גויים to show them his friend's property. He had made him pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה happened to come to בי אביוני. He came before רבא, who asked him: did any case come before you? He answered: a Jew whom גויים forced, and he showed them his friend's property, came before me, and I made him pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of someone who points out another person's property to robbers, and tells a real case. This sets up רבא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is that the man was forced (אנסוהו) and only showed the property. He did not hand it over himself. רב הונא בר יהודה still made him pay for the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case that came up
And I made him liable to pay

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי אֶבְיוֹנֵי.
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda happened to come to Bei Avyonei.
phrases.notes: בי אביוני is the name of a place.

phrases.english: He came before Rava,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּלוּם מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִידָךְ?
phrases.english: he said to him: Did any case come to you?
He said to him: A Jew whom gentiles forced,
and he showed them his friend's property,
came to me, and I made him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי אֶבְיוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the קנס discussion is done, and the גמרא goes back to the case of showing someone's property to robbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא בר יהודה made a Jew who was forced to show his friend's property to גויים pay for it.

steps.title: רבא says to reverse the ruling, based on a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב הונא בר יהודה to undo his ruling. A ברייתא says that one who is forced and only shows the property is פטור. Only one who hands it over himself is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: reverse the case and give the money back, because a ברייתא teaches: a Jew whom גויים forced and who showed them his friend's property is exempt. But if he took it and handed it over with his own hand, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב הונא בר יהודה's ruling and proves from a ברייתא that he got it wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws a clear line. When he is forced, just showing the property is פטור. Only actively taking it and handing it over is חייב. Since the man in the case only showed it, he should not have paid.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt; does not have to pay
Took it and handed it over with his own hand

steps.whatToRemember: When forced, only showing the property is פטור. Handing it over with your own hand is חייב.

phrases.english: He said to him: Reverse the case to its owner,
phrases.notes: He means: give the money back to the man you made pay.

phrases.english: as it was taught: A Jew whom gentiles forced
and he showed his friend's property, is exempt;
but if he took and gave it by hand, he is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַהְדַּר עוֹבָדָא לְמָרֵיהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling that רב הונא בר יהודה reported in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר יהודה's ruling that the forced Jew must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a forced Jew who only shows the property is exempt, and that is exactly what happened in this case.

steps.title: Showing it on his own counts like handing it over
steps.stepSummary: רבה adds that if he showed the property on his own, without being forced, it is like handing it over with his own hand. So he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: if he showed it on his own, it is as if he took it and handed it over with his own hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds a limit to the ברייתא. The exemption only applies when he was forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא exempted showing only because he was forced. If nobody forced him and he pointed out the property by himself, that is treated like actively handing it over, so he must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: On his own, without being forced

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the ברייתא as saying showing is always פטור. It is פטור only when he was forced. Showing on his own is חייב.
steps.whatToRemember: Forced and only showed: פטור. Handed it over himself: חייב. Showed it on his own: also חייב.

phrases.english: Rabba said: If he showed it on his own,
it is as if he took and gave it by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא from step 13: its exemption is only when he was forced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Showing someone's property to robbers on one's own is treated like handing it over, so he must pay.

steps.title: A man forced to show and carry רב מרי's wine is exempted
steps.stepSummary: גויים force a man to show them רב מרי's wine and then make him carry it for them. רב אשי rules that he does not have to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man whom גויים forced, and he showed them the wine of רב מרי son of רב פנחס son of רב חסדא. They said to him, 'Carry it and bring it with us,' and he did. The case came before רב אשי, and he ruled that the man was exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. A forced man first showed the wine and then carried it himself, and רב אשי said he does not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case goes beyond the earlier ones. In step 13, only someone who hands the property over himself is חייב, and here the man did carry it with his own hands. Even so, רב אשי exempts him, so the next steps will ask why.

phrases.english: There was a certain man whom gentiles forced,
and he showed them the wine

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב פִּנְחָס בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא.
phrases.english: of Rav Mari, son of Rav Pinchas, son of Rav Chisda.
They said to him: "Carry it and bring it with us,"
and he carried it and brought it with them.
The case came before Rav Ashi, and he exempted him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new story that seems to clash with the ברייתא in step 13, which says handing over by hand makes one חייב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who was forced to show property and then carried it for the גויים is פטור.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רב אשי: handing over by hand makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out that a ברייתא says one who carries and hands over property is חייב, and that is exactly what this man did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to רב אשי: But a ברייתא teaches that if he took the property and handed it over by hand, he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רב אשי's ruling using the ברייתא we saw earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws the line between only showing (פטור) and physically handing over (חייב). This man physically carried the wine, so by the ברייתא he should pay.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it taught in a ברייתא
took and handed over by hand

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Ashi:
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
If he took it and handed it over by hand, he is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב אָשֵׁי, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's ruling in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's exemption of the man who carried the wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes one who physically hands over property חייב, and this man physically carried it.

steps.title: Once he showed it, the damage was already done
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ברייתא applies only where he did not first lead the גויים to the property. Here he showed it first, so the loss already happened then.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: That rule applies when he did not bring them to the property from the start. But when he brought them to it from the start, it is as if he already burned it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by limiting when the ברייתא applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גויים never knew about the property, handing it over is what causes the loss, so he is חייב. Here the property was already lost the moment he showed it, and he was forced to do that, so he was פטור. Carrying it afterward did not cause any new loss.

keyTerms.meaning: he already burned it (the loss already happened)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב אשי is arguing with the ברייתא. He agrees that handing over makes one חייב. He only says that here the handing over came after the property was already lost.

phrases.english: He said to them: That applies
where he did not bring them to it from the start,
but where he brought them to it from the start,
he already burned it.
phrases.notes: Literally 'burned, he burned it.' Once he showed them the wine, it was as good as gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא אוֹקְמֵיהּ עִילָּוֵיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any physical handing over makes one חייב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Handing over makes one חייב only if it is what causes the loss. If the property was already lost through forced showing, he is פטור.

steps.title: רבי אבהו challenges: passing an item to a robber who is right there
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a ברייתא where an אנס, who is already present, says 'pass me this,' and the one who passes it is still חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו challenged רב אשי: If an אנס said to someone, 'Pass me this bundle of grain or this cluster of grapes,' and he passed it to him, he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו raises a new challenge to רב אשי from a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אנס is standing right there and can already see the item, so the item seems already lost, just like the wine. Yet the ברייתא says the one who passes it is חייב. This seems to go against רב אשי's idea that handing over adds nothing once the property is already exposed.

keyTerms.meaning: a robber, someone who takes by force

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu challenged Rav Ashi:
If a robber said to him:
"Pass me this bundle of grain,
or this cluster of grapes,"
and he passed it to him, he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that handing over property that is already exposed adds no liability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אנס already has access to the item, yet the one who passes it is still חייב.

steps.title: The robber was across the river
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that in the ברייתא, the two people stood on opposite sides of a river, so the אנס could not reach the item himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? One where they stand on two sides of a river.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבי אבהו by explaining the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Across a river, the אנס could see the item but could not take it. The passing is what actually caused the loss, so the one who passed it is חייב. This fits רב אשי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
A case where they stand on two sides of a river.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אנס was standing right next to the item, so it was already exposed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אנס could not reach it, so passing it is what caused the loss.

steps.title: The wording 'pass' and not 'give' proves the river case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב אשי's reading from the wording of the ברייתא. It says 'pass,' which means reaching over a distance, and not 'give.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since the ברייתא says 'pass' and not 'give.' Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב אשי's explanation from the exact word the ברייתא uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Pass' suggests the item had to be reached across to someone who could not get it himself. If the אנס were right there, the ברייתא would have said 'give.' So the wording itself shows the ברייתא is talking about a case where the אנס had no access.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also precise (it supports this)

steps.whatToRemember: A forced Jew who shows property and then carries it is פטור, because the loss already happened when he showed it. Handing over makes one חייב only when it is what actually causes the loss, like passing an item across a river to an אנס who could not reach it.

phrases.english: The wording is also precise,
since it teaches "pass"
and does not teach "give";
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 19 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's explanation that the ברייתא is about a river case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's choice of the word הושיט ('pass') instead of תן ('give')

steps.title: Two people fight over a net, and one hands it to the king's officer
steps.stepSummary: A new case: two people both claim a net, and one of them gives it to a government officer.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a net that two people were fighting over. Each one said, 'It is mine.' One of them went and handed it over to the king's officer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story to set up a question. Two people both claim a net, and one of them hands it to a government official.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes this case different from the earlier ones is that nobody knows who really owns the net. The question that follows is whether the one who handed it over has to pay, since he might have given away his own net.

phrases.english: There was a certain net
that two people were quarreling over.
This one said: It is mine,
and that one said: It is mine.
One of them went
and handed it over to an officer of the king.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, giving the full spelling of the word for the king's officer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא שׁוּתָא דַּהֲווֹ מִנְּצוּ עֲלַהּ בֵּי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about handing property to the authorities, this time where ownership is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case: a net whose ownership is in dispute is handed by one claimant to a royal officer.

steps.title: אביי says he can claim he gave away his own net
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the one who handed it over is exempt, because he can say the net was his.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He can say, 'When I handed it over, I handed over what was mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his ruling: the one who handed over the net does not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody has proven the net belongs to the other person, the one who handed it over can claim he only gave away his own property. Nobody can prove otherwise, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: He is able to say (he has a valid claim)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He can say:
When I handed it over, I handed over what is mine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first ruling on the net case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who handed over the disputed net is exempt, since he can claim it was his own.

steps.title: רבא asks: is it up to him to decide?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: the man cannot settle the dispute on his own by giving the net away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Is it really up to him?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's ruling with a sharp question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The net is still under dispute, so neither side is allowed to act as if it is clearly his. By handing it to the government, the man took the other person's chance to win in court. So his claim 'it was mine' does not protect him.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it in his power? (Can he decide this by himself?)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
And is it up to him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's ruling directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the man can say he gave away his own net.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: While ownership is still in dispute, one side cannot decide it for himself. Giving the net away destroys the other side's chance to win in court.

steps.title: רבא rules: put him in שמתא until he brings the net to court
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own ruling: we put the man in שמתא until he gets the net back and goes to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: We put him in שמתא until he brings the net back and stands in court.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting אביי, רבא gives his own ruling on the net case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not simply make the man pay, because it is still unclear who owns the net. Instead, the בית דין pressures him with שמתא until he brings the net back. Then the case can be judged properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier view and giving a new one)
We put him in שמתא (a form of excommunication)
And he stands in judgment (goes to court)

steps.whatToRemember: When ownership is disputed, one side may not hand the item to the authorities and then claim it was his. רבא says we put him in שמתא until he restores the item and goes to court.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
We excommunicate him
until he brings it back
and stands in judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected ruling with רבא's own ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who handed over the disputed item is put in שמתא until he brings it back and goes to court.

steps.title: A man insists he will inform on his fellow's straw, even against רב
steps.stepSummary: A man wants to show his fellow's straw to the authorities. רב forbids it, and the man refuses to listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who wanted to point out his fellow's straw to the authorities. He came before רב, who told him, 'Don't show it, don't show it!' The man answered, 'I will show it, I will show it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a מוסר, a person who informs on a fellow Jew's property. This sets up what רב כהנא does next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב repeats 'don't show it' to make the ban as strong as possible. The man answers with the same doubled words, showing he fully means to go ahead. This makes it clear that he is about to cause the loss and cannot be talked out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: To show / point out (to the authorities)

phrases.english: There was a certain man
who wanted to show his fellow's straw.
phrases.notes: He wanted to point it out to the gentile officials so they would take it.

phrases.english: He came before Rav.
He said to him: "Do not show it, and do not show it!"
He said to him: "I will show it, and I will show it!"

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה בָּעֵי אַחְווֹיֵי אַתִּיבְנָא דְחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about a person who insists on informing on his fellow's property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב forbids informing on a fellow Jew's property; the man openly refuses.

steps.title: רב כהנא kills the informer
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא, sitting before רב, breaks the man's neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא was sitting before רב, and he broke the man's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רב כהנא responds to the man's refusal by killing him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man had just said clearly that he would hand over his fellow's property to the authorities. רב כהנא acted right away to stop him. The next step explains why רב saw this as justified.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as permission for anyone to harm a person for any reason. The story is about a man who openly declared he would hand a Jew's property to the authorities, and the next step gives רב's reason.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana was sitting before Rav;
he pulled the man's neck out from him.
phrases.notes: He broke the man's neck and killed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with רב כהנא's reaction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא kills the man who insisted on informing.

steps.title: רב uses a פסוק to show why רב כהנא acted rightly
steps.stepSummary: רב reads a פסוק comparing a Jew's money in gentile hands to an antelope caught in a net, which gets no mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב read this פסוק about him: 'Your sons have fainted, they lie at the head of every street, like an antelope in a net.' Just as no one has mercy on an antelope once it falls into a net, so too once a Jew's money falls into the hands of gentiles, no mercy is shown to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב backs up רב כהנא's action with a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison shows how serious informing is. Once property is handed to those authorities, there is no getting it back and no mercy for the owner. So the informer was not causing a small loss. He was putting a fellow Jew in grave danger, which justifies stopping him.

keyTerms.meaning: They have no mercy on him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the very harsh treatment of a מוסר. Handing a Jew's property to oppressive authorities is treated as a danger to the Jew himself, not just a money matter.

phrases.english: Rav read about him:
"Your sons have fainted, they lie
at the head of all the streets, like an antelope in a net";
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 51:20

phrases.english: Just as this antelope,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּפַל בְּמִכְמָר – אֵין מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו;
phrases.english: once it falls into a net, no one has mercy on it;
so too the money of a Jew,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּפַל בְּיַד גּוֹיִם – אֵין מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: once it falls into the hands of gentiles, no mercy is shown to him.
phrases.notes: "Him" here is the Jew himself. Once they go after his money, they will not spare him either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's justification for רב כהנא's act.
steps.raayaObject: That רב כהנא acted properly in stopping the informer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 51:20, comparing a Jew's money in gentile hands to an antelope caught in a net.

steps.title: רב tells רב כהנא to flee to ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב warns that the new rulers punish killing, and sends רב כהנא to ארץ ישראל to learn from רבי יוחנן without challenging him for seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: 'כהנא, until now the Persians ruled, and they did not care about killing. Now there are Greeks, who do care about killing, and they will say, "Murder, murder!" Get up and go up to ארץ ישראל, and accept upon yourself not to challenge רבי יוחנן for seven years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב sending רב כהנא away for his own safety.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the act was justified in Jewish law, the new rulers would treat it as murder and punish רב כהנא. So רב tells him to leave. He also adds a condition for his learning in ארץ ישראל: for seven years he must not ask challenges against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: That you will not raise difficulties

steps.whatToRemember: רב approved of stopping the informer, but because the new rulers would see it as murder, he sent רב כהנא to ארץ ישראל to learn under רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rav said to him: "Kahana,
until now there were Persians,
who were not strict about bloodshed;
but now there are Greeks
who are strict about bloodshed,
and they will say: 'Murder, murder!'
Get up and go up to Eretz Yisrael,
and accept upon yourself

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא תַּקְשֵׁי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן שֶׁבַע שְׁנִין״.
phrases.english: that you will not raise difficulties to Rabbi Yochanan for seven years."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב: כָּהֲנָא, עַד הָאִידָּנָא הֲווֹ פָּרְסָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with רב's practical advice after justifying the act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the new rulers punish killing, רב כהנא must flee to ארץ ישראל and not challenge רבי יוחנן for seven years.

steps.title: רב כהנא impresses ריש לקיש, who calls him a lion
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא finds ריש לקיש reviewing the daily lesson and shows he has questions and answers. ריש לקיש tells רבי יוחנן that a 'lion' has come from בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and found ריש לקיש sitting and reviewing the day's lesson for the students. He asked them: Where is ריש לקיש? They asked: Why? He said: I have this question and that question, and this answer and that answer. They told ריש לקיש. ריש לקיש went and told רבי יוחנן: A lion has come up from בבל. Let the Master prepare tomorrow's lesson carefully.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רב כהנא arrives in ארץ ישראל, and ריש לקיש quickly sees how sharp he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's questions and answers on the review show his strength. ריש לקיש is himself a great questioner, so his calling רב כהנא a 'lion' is high praise. It also sets up the tension, because רב told רב כהנא not to challenge רבי יוחנן for seven years.

keyTerms.meaning: The lesson or session in the בית מדרש
Lion, a nickname for a very great scholar

phrases.english: He went, and found Reish Lakish
phrases.notes: "He" is רב כהנא, who was just sent to ארץ ישראל in Step 28.

phrases.english: who was sitting and reviewing
the day's lesson for the students.
phrases.notes: This means ריש לקיש was going over רבי יוחנן's daily lesson with the students.

phrases.english: He said to them: Where is Reish Lakish?
They said to him: Why?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הַאי קוּשְׁיָא וְהַאי קוּשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: He said to them: This difficulty and that difficulty,
and this resolution and that resolution.
They told Reish Lakish.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish went and said to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
"A lion has come up from Babylonia;
let the Master look carefully into tomorrow's lesson."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רב sends רב כהנא to ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש recognizes רב כהנא as a 'lion' and warns רבי יוחנן to prepare.

steps.title: רב כהנא stays silent and is moved back seven rows
steps.stepSummary: Seated in the front row, רב כהנא keeps רב's instruction and asks nothing. He is moved back row by row to the last row, and רבי יוחנן says the 'lion' has become a 'fox.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day they seated him in the first row, in front of רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן said a teaching, and he did not challenge. Another teaching, and he did not challenge. They moved him back seven rows until he sat in the last row. רבי יוחנן said to ריש לקיש: The lion you spoke of has become a fox!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא obeys רב's command not to challenge רבי יוחנן, so everyone thinks he is weak and he is moved to the back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this בית מדרש, seating followed a student's strength in asking questions. Silence looked like ignorance, so each teaching without a question sent רב כהנא back one row. The 'fox' remark is the opposite of ריש לקיש's 'lion.'
steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is not silent because he has no questions. He is keeping רב's instruction not to challenge רבי יוחנן for seven years (Step 28).

phrases.english: The next day they seated him in the first row
in front of Rabbi Yoḥanan.
He said a teaching, and he did not challenge;
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן says the teaching, and רב כהנא is the one who stays quiet.

phrases.english: a teaching, and he did not challenge;
they moved him back seven rows,
until they seated him in the last row.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
"The lion you spoke of has become a fox!"

steps.triggerLanguage: לִמְחַר אוֹתְבוּהּ בְּדָרָא קַמָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened at the lesson ריש לקיש warned about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping רב's instruction, רב כהנא is silent and loses his place, falling to the last row.

steps.title: Seven rows in place of seven years; רב כהנא begins asking
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא prays that the seven rows count instead of רב's seven years. He asks רבי יוחנן to start over, raises difficulties, and is returned to the first row.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: May it be God's will that these seven rows count in place of the seven years that רב told me. He stood up and said: Let the Master go back to the beginning. רבי יוחנן said a teaching, and he challenged. They put him in the first row. He said a teaching, and he challenged.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא finds a way to honor רב's instruction: seven rows of being lowered stand in for seven years. Then he finally starts asking questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the turning point of the story. Being moved back seven times is treated as a 'payment' for the seven years of silence. Once he starts asking, his strength shows right away and he goes back to the front.

phrases.english: He said: May it be the will
phrases.notes: This is רב כהנא speaking, probably to himself, as a short prayer.

phrases.english: that these seven rows
should be in place of the seven years
that Rav told me.
He stood on his feet and said to him:
"Let the Master go back to the beginning."
He said a teaching, and he challenged.
They placed him in the first row.
He said a teaching, and he challenged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: יְהֵא רַעֲוָא דְּהָנֵי שְׁבַע דָּרֵי לִהְווֹ חִילּוּף שְׁבַע שְׁנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses Step 30: the silent 'fox' now shows he is a 'lion.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven rows replace seven years. רב כהנא starts challenging and returns to the first row.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's cushions are removed one by one
steps.stepSummary: For each strong question from רב כהנא, a cushion is pulled out from under רבי יוחנן, until he is sitting on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן was sitting on seven cushions. They pulled one cushion out from under him. He said a teaching and רב כהנא challenged him, until they had pulled all the cushions out from under him and he was sitting on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows how powerful רב כהנא's questions were: each one lowers רבי יוחנן by one cushion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven cushions match the seven rows. רב כהנא was lowered seven times by being silent, and now רבי יוחנן is lowered seven times by רב כהנא's questions.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה יָתֵיב אַשְּׁבַע בִּסְתַּרְקֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan was sitting on seven cushions,
they pulled one cushion out from under him.
He said a teaching, and he challenged him,

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּשָׁלְפִי לֵיהּ כּוּלְּהוּ בִּסְתַּרְקֵי מִתּוּתֵיהּ,
phrases.english: until they pulled all the cushions out from under him,
until he was sitting on the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה יָתֵיב אַשְּׁבַע בִּסְתַּרְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the questioning that began in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא's questions bring רבי יוחנן down from seven cushions to the ground.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks to have his eyes uncovered to see רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was old and his eyebrows hung over his eyes. He asks that they be lifted so he can see רב כהנא, and they lift them with a silver brush.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן was an old man, and his eyebrows drooped. He said to them: Lift up my eyes for me and I will see him. They lifted them for him with a silver eye brush.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן wants to look at this amazing student. The גמרא is setting up what happens when he sees him, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After being beaten in argument, רבי יוחנן wants to see רב כהנא for himself. This detail leads straight into the next part of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: An eye brush, a stick for eye makeup

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan was an old man
and his eyebrows drooped,
he said to them: Lift up my eyes for me
phrases.notes: He means: lift the eyebrows that are covering my eyes.

phrases.english: and I will see him.
They lifted them for him with a silver eye brush.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן גַּבְרָא סָבָא הֲוָה וּמְסָרְחִי גְּבִינֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רבי יוחנן's defeat in argument. He now wants to see the student who beat him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן asks to have his eyes uncovered so he can see רב כהנא. This sets up the next scene.

steps.title: A split lip is mistaken for mocking, and רב כהנא dies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן sees רב כהנא's split lips and thinks he is laughing at him. רבי יוחנן is hurt, and רב כהנא dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן saw that רב כהנא's lips were split and thought he was laughing at him. רבי יוחנן felt hurt, and רב כהנא died.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that he can finally see, רבי יוחנן misreads רב כהנא's face as a mocking smile. He feels hurt, and רב כהנא dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole tragedy rests on a misunderstanding. רב כהנא did nothing wrong on purpose; his lips just looked that way. Still, the hurt of a great teacher has a deadly effect.

keyTerms.meaning: He felt hurt or offended (literally, his mind became weak)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep track of who is who. רבי יוחנן is the one who sees and feels hurt. רב כהנא is the one with the split lips, and he is the one who dies.

phrases.english: He saw that his lips were split,
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is the one seeing here, now that his eyebrows were lifted. The lips belong to רב כהנא.

phrases.english: he thought that he was laughing at him.
He felt hurt, and he died.
phrases.notes: The one who felt hurt is רבי יוחנן. The one who died is רב כהנא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues directly from the lifting of רבי יוחנן's eyebrows: what he sees once he can see.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן misreads רב כהנא's split lips as mocking. He is hurt, and רב כהנא dies.

steps.title: The students explain that רב כהנא always looked that way
steps.stepSummary: The next day רבי יוחנן complains to the students about the Babylonian's behavior. They tell him this was simply how רב כהנא's face naturally looked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day רבי יוחנן said to the Rabbis: Did you see what the Babylonian did? They answered him: That is just how he is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings up what he thinks was disrespect. His students correct him: רב כהנא was not laughing, his face always looked like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This short exchange reveals the misunderstanding. The 'insult' was never real, so רבי יוחנן's hurt, and רב כהנא's death, came from a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: That is his way, that is just how he is

phrases.aramaic: לִמְחַר אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: The next day, Rabbi Yochanan said to the Rabbis:
Did you see what the Babylonian did?
They said to him: That is just how he is.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִמְחַר אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the 'mocking' in the previous step was a misunderstanding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא was never mocking; his face naturally looked that way.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן goes to רב כהנא's burial cave
steps.stepSummary: After learning the truth, רבי יוחנן goes to רב כהנא's burial cave and sees something there. The description continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to the burial cave and saw that it was...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reacts to learning his mistake by going to רב כהנא's burial cave. This line sets up the next part of the story, which tells what he saw there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that he knows רב כהנא was innocent, רבי יוחנן goes to his grave. The sentence breaks off here, and what he finds at the cave comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He went in or went to

phrases.english: He went to the cave,
phrases.notes: This is the cave where רב כהנא was buried.

phrases.english: he saw that it was

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן's response after the students explain that רב כהנא was not mocking him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן goes to רב כהנא's burial cave; the story continues.
